plan.disposition: mid-flight small-to-medium escalation (references/mid-flight-escalation.md): the backfill checklist requires only external LLM review before further code changes, not a separate Branch A plan/architecture review — that gate belongs to the fresh medium-complexity flow this run bypassed by escalating after Build had already started

findings.finding: ActivityCard.subrunnerId's doc comment still described the disproven initial hand-back-message design instead of the corrected provisional-id/ack-overwrite/task-notification design.
findings.suggestion: Update the field doc to describe the corrected mechanism.

findings.finding: The corrected subrunner resolution mechanism (extractSubrunnerAgentId, applySubrunnerAck, resolveSubrunnerNotification) had essentially no direct test coverage, and no reducer-level test exercised the harness's real dispatch tool name 'Agent' at all.
findings.suggestion: Add unit tests directly against missionActivityFeedSubrunner.ts's exports covering dispatch -> ack -> task-notification, plus one end-to-end test using tool name 'Agent'.

findings.finding: No test covered the new subrunner rendering branch (running dot, resolved report-link button, inline-fallback).
findings.suggestion: Add MissionActivityFeedCard.test.tsx cases for all three subrunner render states.

findings.finding: New SubrunnerPanel component had no dedicated test file, and MissionBody.test.tsx had no case for the new activeNode = subrunner:<id> wiring.
findings.suggestion: Add SubrunnerPanel.test.tsx and a MissionBody.test.tsx case that opens the panel from a resolved subrunner card.

findings.finding: The one PR-card test unknowingly exercised the new item-1 dedup-suppression path but asserted nothing about it; no companion test proved a genuinely different narrative sentence stays visible.
findings.suggestion: Add positive/negative assertions for the PR-title dedup suppression.

findings.finding: The subrunner PendingTool.commandKey was hardcoded to the 'Agent' literal even when tool.name === 'Task', inconsistent with every other bucket in the file.
findings.suggestion: Use tool.name instead of the hardcoded literal.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: a non-review Task dispatch resolves through the same ack->notification path as an Agent dispatch and eventually reaches subrunnerStatus done/failed — The classic Claude Code Task tool is synchronous — its own tool_result IS the subagent's final answer. A non-review Task falls into the subrunner bucket, whose ack handling only recognized the Agent-style async ack shape (agentId: <id>). A synchronous Task's tool_result would essentially never contain that string, so subrunnerId would stay the provisional tool_use.id forever and no task-notification would ever arrive for a Task that already completed synchronously — the card would get stuck permanently at subrunnerStatus: running, silently discarding the real report.
findings.suggestion: either empirically confirm a non-review Task's completion also arrives via task-notification, or handle a non-review Task's ack synchronously — read result.content directly as the finished report and mark the card done/failed on ack.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the ack (which overwrites subrunnerId to the real, stable agent id) always finishes processing before any task-notification for that same task is processed — resolveSubrunnerNotification correlates strictly by event.taskId === card.subrunnerId at the moment the notification event is walked, with no retry/rescan queue. No mechanism nor test proved the ack event is guaranteed to be seen and applied before the notification event within a single derivation pass.
findings.suggestion: a written argument for why ack-before-notification ordering is structurally guaranteed within one JSONL transcript, or a fallback re-attempt mechanism.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: AGENT_ID_RE only ever matches the harness's own launch-acknowledgement preamble — The regex was an unanchored substring search over the entire ack content. Any ack content that happened to contain the literal text 'agentId: <token>' for unrelated reasons could silently overwrite subrunnerId with a garbage value, permanently breaking correlation.
findings.suggestion: anchor the regex to the known preamble so an incidental substring in unrelated prose can't be mistaken for the dispatch's own id fingerprint.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: resolveSubrunnerNotification's cards.find() correctly resolves exactly the one card a notification is for — .find() returns only the first matching open subrunner card, with no defense against two concurrently-open subrunner cards ever sharing a subrunnerId.
findings.suggestion: prefer the still-running card with that id over an already-resolved one, so a collision degrades predictably rather than picking array order.

findings.finding: Item 1 specifies suppressing a sentence that duplicates the PR box title — implying sentence-level stripping. The implementation only suppresses when the entire `card.text` equals the synthesized `Merged as "X".` string. If the narrative text is `"Investigated the flaky test. Merged as \"X\"."` (duplicate sentence plus other real content), the duplicate sentence still renders. Conversely, the "near-exact" tolerance from the AC (e.g. trailing-whitespace or period variants) is also unimplemented.
findings.suggestion: Split `card.text` into sentences (or match the duplicate as a substring with a regex tolerant of punctuation/whitespace) and strip only the matching sentence, rendering the remainder.

findings.finding: The original failure mode (a multi-KB report silently failing the `endsWith` check, leaving the subrunner card stuck on "running" forever) was not fixed, only moved: any notification whose envelope exceeds 64 KB now returns `null` at the very first line, so the event is dropped entirely and the card is permanently stuck on `"running"` with no report. The Confidence Calibration section itself documents reports that "ran several KB," so this is a realistic input class, not hypothetical.
findings.suggestion: On oversized content, don't bail before parsing — at minimum still extract `status`/`task-id`/`summary` (truncating `result`) so the card resolves; the `startsWith`/`endsWith` envelope check can also be relaxed (e.g. `lastIndexOf("</task-notification>")`) so a trailing newline or truncated tail doesn't kill the whole event.

findings.finding: The spec says "the PR-number span gets `flex-shrink: 0`". The implementation pins whichever span happens to be the first child of `.mc-feed-pr-meta`. This is positional and fragile — a JSX reorder of the merge-state/PR-number spans (or insertion of a new leading span) silently pins the wrong element, reintroducing exactly the clipping this item fixes. Add a test or a dedicated class.
findings.suggestion: Give the PR-number span its own class (e.g. `.mc-feed-pr-num`) and target that instead of `:first-child`.

findings.finding: The divider test only asserts the time portion (`toLocaleTimeString`) is present, and never checks the date/"Today" segment, the "Session started ·" prefix, or that the divider appears above the first card. A broken `formatSessionStart` that returns only a time string, or a divider rendered at the bottom, still passes.
findings.suggestion: Assert the full rendered text (e.g. via a fixed fake-timers date so "Today, 09:15" is deterministic) and assert the divider precedes the first card entry.

findings.finding: If `card.subrunnerId` changes while the panel is open (the reducer can overwrite it mid-lifecycle), the capture effect re-runs and overwrites `returnToRef` with the panel's own close button, so focus is restored to a dead element on unmount rather than the original trigger. Minor a11y regression path, not a crash.
findings.suggestion: Only capture on mount (empty dep array), or guard against capturing an element inside the panel.
